newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria state under curfew after tribal fighting.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria state under curfew after tribal fighting.

text.p: A curfew has been imposed on the central Nigerian state of Plateau where more than 25 people have been killed from ethnic clashes this week, the independent Thisday newspaper reported on Saturday.
Plateau state military administrator Colonel Habibu Shuaibu announced on Friday that the curfew would apply from 9 p.m. (2000 GMT) until dawn.
He was speaking in Gero village where 15 people were killed on Thursday when residents attacked immigrant farmers.
Around 70 other people were injured in the fighting at Gero between ethnic Beroms and Hausa immigrants -- the second eruption of violence in four days.
Eight people were killed at Changai, in the same Plateau State, on Monday when another two communities clashed with bows and arrows over a traditional ceremony.
Shuaibu said the recent violence in the state was shameful and barbaric and his government would deal ruthlessly with anyone encouraging communal violence, Thisday reported.
Tribal violence is common in Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation with more than 100 million people and 250 ethnic groups.
